# infisical_sso_oidc (Resource)

Manage the OIDC SSO configuration of the organization. An organization has at most one OIDC configuration, and it belongs to the organization of the machine identity. Set either `discovery_url` or `custom`. A change to `discovery_url`, `custom`, `client_id`, the client secret, `allowed_email_domains`, `jwt_signature_algorithm` or `is_active` turns off SSO enforcement and SCIM for the organization in Infisical, and destroying this resource turns them off too. A change to `manage_group_memberships`, `mfa_claim_name` or `mfa_amr_values` alone keeps them on. Older Infisical versions turn them off on any update that changes an attribute other than `mfa_claim_name` and `mfa_amr_values`. Only Machine Identity authentication is supported for this resource, and only for a root organization: sub-organizations cannot manage SSO.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    infisical = {
      # version = <latest version>
      source = "infisical/infisical"
    }
  }
}

provider "infisical" {
  host = "https://app.infisical.com" # Only required if using self hosted instance of Infisical, default is https://app.infisical.com
  auth = {
    universal = {
      client_id     = "<machine-identity-client-id>"
      client_secret = "<machine-identity-client-secret>"
    }
  }
}

variable "oidc_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# Users can log in through OIDC only with an email domain that the organization has verified.
resource "infisical_email_domain" "example" {
  domain = "example.com"
}

# Publish verification_record_name and verification_code as a DNS TXT record with your DNS provider,
# and add that record to depends_on here.
resource "infisical_email_domain_verification" "example" {
  email_domain_id = infisical_email_domain.example.id
}

# An identity provider with a discovery endpoint.
resource "infisical_sso_oidc" "example" {
  discovery_url = "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration"
  client_id     = "<oidc-client-id>"

  # Write-only: the secret is not stored in state. Requires Terraform 1.11 or later.
  # Increment client_secret_wo_version when the secret changes.
  client_secret_wo         = var.oidc_client_secret
  client_secret_wo_version = 1

  allowed_email_domains = ["example.com"]
  is_active             = true

  # Changing only the MFA attributes keeps SSO enforcement on.
  mfa_amr_values = ["otp", "hwk"]

  # Configure OIDC after the domain is verified.
  depends_on = [infisical_email_domain_verification.example]
}

# An identity provider without a discovery endpoint.
# resource "infisical_sso_oidc" "custom" {
#   custom = {
#     issuer                 = "https://idp.example.com"
#     authorization_endpoint = "https://idp.example.com/authorize"
#     token_endpoint         = "https://idp.example.com/token"
#     jwks_uri               = "https://idp.example.com/jwks"
#     userinfo_endpoint      = "https://idp.example.com/userinfo"
#   }
#   client_id     = "<oidc-client-id>"
#   client_secret = var.oidc_client_secret
#   is_active     = true
#
#   depends_on = [infisical_email_domain_verification.example]
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) The client ID to use for OIDC authentication.

### Optional

- `allowed_email_domains` (Set of String) The email domains that can log in through this configuration, for example `example.com`. When empty, every domain can log in.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) The client secret to use for OIDC authentication. Exactly one of `client_secret` and `client_secret_wo` must be set.
- `client_secret_wo` (String, Sensitive) The client secret to use for OIDC authentication, as a write-only value that is not stored in state. Exactly one of `client_secret` and `client_secret_wo` must be set. Requires Terraform version 1.11.0 or higher.
- `client_secret_wo_version` (Number) Used together with `client_secret_wo` to trigger an update. Increment this value when `client_secret_wo` changes.
- `custom` (Attributes) The OIDC endpoints, for an identity provider without a discovery endpoint. Exactly one of `discovery_url` and `custom` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--custom))
- `discovery_url` (String) The URL of the OIDC discovery endpoint. Infisical reads the issuer and the endpoints from it. Exactly one of `discovery_url` and `custom` must be set.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether this OIDC configuration is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `jwt_signature_algorithm` (String) The algorithm to use for JWT signature verification. One of `RS256`, `HS256`, `RS512` or `EdDSA`. Defaults to `RS256`.
- `manage_group_memberships` (Boolean) Whether Infisical syncs the user's group memberships from the groups claim at each login. Defaults to `false`.
- `mfa_amr_values` (Set of String) Additional MFA claim values, besides `mfa`, that prove the identity provider completed MFA. At most 20 values.
- `mfa_claim_name` (String) The ID token claim that lists the authentication methods the user completed. Defaults to `amr`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the OIDC configuration.

<a id="nestedatt--custom"></a>
### Nested Schema for `custom`

Required:

- `authorization_endpoint` (String) The authorization endpoint of the identity provider.
- `issuer` (String) The issuer of the identity provider.
- `jwks_uri` (String) The URL of the OIDC JWKS endpoint.
- `token_endpoint` (String) The token endpoint to use for OIDC token exchange.
- `userinfo_endpoint` (String) The userinfo endpoint to get user information from the OIDC provider.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# This will import the OIDC configuration by the ID of the organization. An organization has at most one OIDC configuration.
terraform import infisical_sso_oidc.example <organization_id>
```
